identityReview: Matched Stanford electrical-engineering alumna, former Google Ethical AI co-lead and DAIR founder across university biographies, papers, award organizer and current event reporting. Birth year 1983 follows the Right Livelihood laureate profile; no exact birthday asserted.
lifeStatusEvidence: AfroTech post-event reporting published November 4 and updated November 5 explicitly identifies her speaking in Houston on Tuesday November 3, 2026. This is an observed event report, not a future speaker listing.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read PMLR and arXiv records, full AfroTech report, award announcement and laureate profile, Stanford and Caltech biographies, university-hosted original ACM paper, full syndicated Reuters article, Black in AI about page, Chicago biography and publisher listing.

corrections: Stanford electrical-engineering degrees corroborated by Chicago biography; 2017 PhD and Fei-Fei Li supervision corroborated by Caltech and Stanford laboratory alumni. Historical employment listings are not current appointments.

Gender Shades evaluates three historical commercial gender classifiers. It does not establish performance of every face-recognition system or current model versions. Joy Buolamwini coauthorship retained.
Datasheets first arXiv submission is March 23, 2018; journal version is December 2021. Six coauthors retained as a collective contribution.

Stochastic Parrots formal conference publication is March 2021, distinct from the draft involved in the 2020 dispute. Four published bylines and shared contribution retained; Shmargaret Shmitchell is the credited name.
Reuters reports Gebru saying fired and Google saying resignation accepted. These are attributed competing accounts, not an adjudicated legal finding or independently proved motive.
Black in AI dates membership founding to 2017 and nonprofit status to 2018. Rediet Abebe cofounding retained; no assertion that Gebru is its current CEO or president.
DAIR launch December 2, 2021 corroborated by Stanford and Right Livelihood. Direct institute page was inaccessible; no claim to have read it.

Right Livelihood announcement September 30, 2026 is distinct from planned December 1 ceremony. Announcement contains apparent editorial placeholders L4; these were excluded and biography independently compared with the separate laureate profile.
AfroTech reporting date November 4/5 differs from actual November 3 speaking date. Opinions remain attributed; no unverified wage, funding percentage or citation-count assertion.
Publisher lists Deep Unlearning for February 16, 2027. Excluded from completed-event timeline even though contemporary reporting calls her its author.
Original ACM paper read through UC Davis mirror after publisher and Washington-hosted requests failed. Restricted Caltech video not viewed; biographies read as text.
